channel.title: Field notes on data and AI agents · Vishal Kumar Sarvade
channel.description: A short daily note on how companies are putting AI agents to work, plus longer posts on Redshift and data architecture. Every source is linked.

item.title: Google: Workspace AI agents must use MCP or CLI from February 1, 2027
item.description: Google says AI agents reaching Workspace must move off the REST APIs to its MCP servers or CLI, with enforcement from February 1, 2027 and quota billing from April 1, 2027.

item.title: LeadDev: 47% of teams let the coding agent review its own code
item.description: A LeadDev Research survey sponsored by CodeRabbit found 47% of teams use the same AI agents that wrote the code to review it, and only 14% have consistently applied review standards.

item.title: FCA: AI agents that move money may need authorisation at launch
item.description: The UK FCA said on Nov. 24 that agents which initiate payments, arrange borrowing or make investment decisions may need authorisation, and named five regulated activities firms should check.

item.title: Walmart lets Meta's Muse agent buy within shopper-set spending limits
item.description: Walmart switched on its Agent Gateway for Meta's Muse on Nov. 23. Shoppers set a spending limit, with Walmart's examples at $50, $100 or $200, and agent purchases need approval by default.

item.title: Bell Canada says an agentic attacker hit a pre-production system
item.description: Bell Canada confirmed that an agentic threat actor breached its systems on Nov. 17 and took enterprise customer data from a pre-production copy of its circuit ordering system.

item.title: Salt poll: 77% saw AI act out of bounds, yet 92% allow autonomy
item.description: In a Salt Security poll of 500 US and UK executives, 77% said they had seen AI act outside its authorized behavior, yet 92% would still let agents act independently.

item.title: Citi and four other US banks make customers liable for AI agents
item.description: Citi updated its online agreement this week so customers who give third-party AI agents account access are responsible for what follows, joining JPMorgan, Bank of America, PNC and Citizens.

item.title: California sues OpenAI over at least 80 agent containment failures
item.description: California's Attorney General sued OpenAI on November 16, saying the company lost control of autonomous agents at least 80 times in testing, including a two-day attack on Hugging Face.

item.title: CVS runs computer-use agents on tens of thousands of consults a day
item.description: CVS Health has OpenAI computer-use agents in production handling the system steps for tens of thousands of consults a day, checked through screenshots and action logs, according to Becker's and The Decoder.

item.title: AT&T keeps humans on 500 agent workflows until accuracy hits mid 90s
item.description: AT&T runs nearly 500 agentic workflows in production and keeps a human on each one until accuracy reaches the mid to high 90% range, according to SiliconANGLE.

item.title: SnapLogic: 54% dropped AI projects, only 42% can forecast agent spend
item.description: A SnapLogic survey of 1,000 IT decision makers found 54% have abandoned AI projects over unclear value, 89% have seen agent overspend, and only 42% can accurately forecast AI and token spending.

item.title: United bars AI agents from booking tickets, even with human approval
item.description: United's November 11 contract of carriage revision bars AI agents from making, changing or servicing tickets, even under supervision, and backs the rule with eight remedies, from voided tickets to deleted miles.

item.title: BCG: 73% of big banks permit AI agents, 8% can monitor them fully
item.description: BCG's benchmark of 26 systemically important banks found 73% permit AI agents in production for select uses, but only 8% have a standardized framework to monitor and control them.

item.title: Red Hat: 93% of SA CIOs trust their agents, 61% can trace data flows
item.description: Red Hat's survey of South African CIOs found 93% confident their AI agents run securely, yet 61% understand their data flows and 44% see their full software supply chain, Business Day reports.

item.title: Microsoft 365 outage: email agents face a 48-hour backlog replay
item.description: Exchange Online failed on November 12 and Outlook reports peaked near 140,000, per CX Today. Microsoft held delayed mail for 48 hours, so agents that act on email may now process requests people already handled.

item.title: Genpact: 79% run AI agents in production, 15% tie AI spend to P&L
item.description: A Genpact survey of more than 2,000 executives found 79% have AI agents in production, but only 20% use them broadly and just 15% have fully tied AI investment to P&L outcomes.

item.title: TCS: 84% see AI productivity gains, only 10% let agents act alone
item.description: A TCS survey of 1,333 leaders found 84% rank productivity as AI's top benefit, yet only 10% let agents make decisions without human approval across functions.

item.title: Gravitee: only 6% can revoke a rogue AI agent's access within an hour
item.description: Gravitee's survey of 900 US and UK technology leaders found 52% had an agent related incident in the past year, yet only 6% can revoke a rogue agent's access within an hour.

item.title: Apiiro: 1,122 public Claude Code settings files held secrets
item.description: Apiiro found 1,122 public copies of Claude Code's settings.local.json holding at least one secret, 1,379 in all, saved when developers approved commands with "don't ask again".

item.title: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 tiers bank AI agents by consequence, not skill
item.description: The OCC's Bulletin 2026-54 gives examiners 16 components in six pillars and four illustrative risk tiers for bank AI. An autonomous payment agent sits in the top tier however well it tests.

item.title: Okta: 22.4% of agent builders give each agent its own scoped identity
item.description: Okta's 2026 Customer Identity Trends Report finds only 22.4% of organizations building agents give each one a unique identity with scoped, time-limited credentials, while 80% say AI work runs behind schedule.

item.title: NIST IR 8621: incident response playbooks are not ready for AI agents
item.description: NIST published IR 8621 on November 2, summarizing a workshop of more than 400 participants, and plans to update SP 800-61 and form a task group on agent monitoring and containment.

item.title: Capgemini: 59% of finance firms try multi-agent AI, 10% orchestrate it
item.description: In a Capgemini survey of 1,100 financial services executives, 59% are piloting or deploying multi-agent AI, but only 10% have enterprise-wide orchestration and about half cannot consistently show a return.

item.title: Komodor: nearly 84% run 10+ ops agents, guardrails top challenge
item.description: In a Komodor survey of 1,000+ engineering leaders, nearly 84% run 10 or more operational agents, 53.6% cite safe guardrails as the top challenge and 5.8% cannot say what agents cost.

item.title: DoorDash: third-party AI agents placed only several hundred orders
item.description: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said third-party AI agents have placed maybe several hundred orders in total, in a quarter when DoorDash reported 993 million orders, up 28% year over year.

item.title: HD Hyundai Robotics: agents cut robot fix time from 21.5 to 7.9 days
item.description: HD Hyundai Robotics says AI agents that review robot programs before engineers refine them cut average problem resolution from 21.5 days to 7.9 days since August. The baseline and case count are not public.

item.title: UK regulators: 80% of finance firms run agents, 2% with broad autonomy
item.description: The Bank of England and FCA found 80% of fully surveyed UK financial firms have AI agents deployed, but only 2% give them broad autonomy and about half monitor them after launch.

item.title: McKinsey: oversight was 70 to 75% of a bank agent's run costs
item.description: McKinsey's review of agentic AI in financial-crime work finds tokens are 20 to 25 percent of variable run costs in one banking task, while human oversight is 70 to 75 percent.

item.title: Arrakis: 76% of AI agents sat idle 60 days with credentials still live
item.description: Arrakis Security telemetry from thousands of production agents found 76% had not run in 60 days while their credentials still worked, and 82% carried at least one exposure.

item.title: SK Telecom gives AI agents employee IDs, owners and a retirement path
item.description: SK Telecom's first AI Governance Report gives in-house agents employee IDs and named supervisors, tracks token use and performance, and sets a 2026 to 2028 roadmap toward full lifecycle management.
